Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No evidence of a portal or mechanism allowing individuals to view their own NINA/digital ID data was found. The APDP law (2013-015) grants citizens the right of access to their personal data, but no dedicated digital ID data-view functionality has been implemented. World Bank Diagnostic (2021) confirms no citizen-facing digital identity services.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: The Ministry of Justice exercises jurisdictional control over civil registration and handles declaratory judgments (supplementary judgments for adults without birth certificates). General judicial oversight exists but no ID-specific judicial mechanisms were documented. DPI Map records no legally binding redress mechanism for the NINA system.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic (2021) found no formal data sharing arrangements or protocols for NINA; data sharing is ad hoc and unprotected. No national data governance framework exists. DPI Map records 'Terms of data storage and sharing available: NO' and 'Data handling terms exist: NO'.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 2013-015 of 21 May 2013 on the Protection of Personal Data is Mali's data protection law. It was amended by Law No. 2017-070 of 18 December 2017 concerning the functioning of the data protection authority (APDP). DPI Map confirms 'National Data Protection Act Exists: YES'.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Autorité de protection des données à caractère personnel (APDP) was established under Law 2013-015 and launched in 2016. It is independently structured and empowered to investigate, subpoena evidence, and impose sanctions. It has 15 members serving 7-year terms. The DPA is funded directly from the state budget.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The NINA card was granted national identity card status equivalent to the Carte Nationale d'Identité (CNI) by Decree 2016-0041/P-RM of February 15, 2016. It is accepted as legal proof of identity for police checks, voter registration, passport applications, and other official transactions.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Legal framework for the NINA system includes: Law No. 06-040 (Aug 11, 2006) establishing the NINA number; Law No. 06-024 (June 28, 2006) governing civil status; Decree 2016-0041 (Feb 15, 2016) granting NINA card national ID status; Electronic transactions law 2016-012 (May 6, 2016). A general legal basis exists though DPI Map notes no specific ID or Civil Registry Act.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The NINA/RAVEC system was built and operated under a contract with French company IDEMIA (formerly Oberthur Technologies), which controlled the civil identification database. In 2023 Mali accused IDEMIA of holding the database 'hostage' over unpaid bills. The junta is attempting to migrate to Malian control but foreign vendors (now Chinese Emptech for passport) still dominate. The new AES passport (Oct 2025) is supplied by China's Emptech—foreign vendor dominance continues.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: No evidence of specific Ministry of Finance oversight over the NINA/digital ID system was found. The system is managed under the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation (MATD) and the Ministry of Security and Civil Protection. World Bank Diagnostic (2021) notes weak whole-of-government coordination and no specific finance ministry role in ID system governance.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The NINA/passport system was operated under a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) contract primarily financed and run by French company IDEMIA. The 2023 crisis arose because the junta could not pay IDEMIA's bills, causing the system to be shut down. The new AES passport is again supplied by foreign vendor Emptech (China). World Bank Diagnostic (2021) identified a financing gap in the civil registration strategy. Primarily external financing.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The RAVEC census (2009–2011) collected one index fingerprint template encoded into the NINA card's encrypted 2D barcode. The NINA card contains photograph and right-index fingerprint. No iris collection documented. DPI Map (2025) flags 'Uses biometrics: NO' for the current NINA system as the NINA slip (post-2018) lacks biometric authentication capability; however, the underlying RAVEC database was built on fingerprint collection, so fingerprints-only is the accurate historical characterisation.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The RAVEC census (2009–2011) built a biometric digital database managed by CTDEC. NINA numbers are electronically assigned and a central digital database exists. However, civil registration (RAVEC/CR) records remain largely paper-based and decentralised; the NINA database itself is digital, making this a mixed (partially digital) system overall, but the core ID database is digital.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Mali's NINA (Numéro d'Identification Nationale) system was established via the biometric RAVEC census (2009–2011) and is fully deployed nationwide. The NINA card received national identity card status by Decree 2016-0041 (Feb 15, 2016). Over 15 million Malians were registered as of October 2016. A new AES biometric passport was launched in October 2025 with Chinese supplier Emptech replacing IDEMIA.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic (2021) found NINA lacks interoperability with other government databases; no formal data exchange arrangements or standards; sharing is ad hoc and unprotected. Data is siloed in individual ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs). DPI Map (2025) does not record interoperability as enabled.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Under WAEMU/BCEAO AML/CFT rules and Mali's Law No. 2016-020, financial institutions must identify customers using valid ID documents such as the national ID card or NINA card. The NINA card is accepted (not exclusively mandatory as other documents also accepted). KYC compliance requires a valid ID but does not mandate the NINA specifically.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The NINA card is free of charge. ICC-CPI Registry (2018) notes that when NINA card issuance was delayed, the 'Fiche individuelle descriptive' (individual descriptive card) was issued free of charge. The traditional national identity card (CNI) has a low fee of approximately 1,000 CFA francs (under USD 2), but the NINA credential itself is no-cost.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The national identity card (CNI) is available to Malian citizens at age 18 (age of majority). The NINA card equivalent status was confirmed by Decree 2016-0041; enrollment is for adults 18+. ICC-CPI Registry (2018) confirms the national identity card is available when citizens turn 18.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Wikipedia's national identity card policy list records Mali's NINA card as 'Compulsory to all Malian citizens.' The NINA card is required to vote, obtain a passport, and access numerous official services. Law No. 06-044 (electoral law) requires NINA card for voting, effectively making it mandatory.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: World Bank Diagnostic (2021) notes NINA enrollment includes residents, refugees (via National Refugee Commission), and internally displaced persons/returnees (via National Social Development Directorate). Foreigners also require ID for SIM registration (passport accepted per Reddit/travel sources). Some non-nationals are eligible but not all categories equally.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: World Bank ID4D Dataset (2018) estimated 76.8% of total population covered (71% of adults); gender gap with 63% women vs 79% men. Malian authorities in 2016 reported 89% of the population had received NINA cards, with over 15 million registered by October 2016. World Bank ID4D 2018 estimate of 4.25 million unregistered. Coverage is in the 70-89% band.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No evidence of systematic or independent security audits of Mali's NINA/digital ID system was found. The 2023 IDEMIA dispute revealed severe digital sovereignty vulnerabilities with the database held by a foreign vendor. No structured security review process, legally mandated audit, or published security assessment was documented. The transition to Emptech (2025) was framed around 'digital sovereignty' rather than security review outcomes.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: World Bank Diagnostic (2021) notes that for social protection programs (e.g., Jigisemejiri) temporary KYC exceptions were made with a Beneficiary Card; legal ID is eventually required. The NINA is accepted for social services but not exclusively mandatory—beneficiary cards and other documents have been used. Plans exist to link health and social services with NINA (OpenClinic-NINA integration announced 2025).
